text_blocks.snippet: Alzheimer's disease is a progressive brain disorder that gradually destroys memory and thinking skills, ultimately impacting the ability to carry out even the simplest tasks. It is the most common form of dementia. While Alzheimer's is not a normal part of aging, the risk increases with age, with most individuals developing it after 65.
snippet_highlighted_words: a progressive brain disorder that gradually destroys memory and thinking skills, ultimately impacting the ability to carry out even the simplest tasks

list.title: Progressive Neurodegeneration:
list.snippet: Alzheimer's involves the gradual death of nerve cells in the brain, starting in areas responsible for memory and gradually spreading to other regions.

list.title: Abnormal Protein Build-up:
list.snippet: The disease is characterized by the abnormal accumulation of proteins, forming plaques (amyloid) and tangles (tau) in and around brain cells.

list.title: Cognitive Decline:
list.snippet: Symptoms include memory loss, difficulty with thinking, reasoning, and language, and changes in behavior and mood.

list.title: Impact on Daily Life:
list.snippet: As the disease progresses, individuals may struggle with daily activities, communication, and even basic self-care.
